title: Clamp
statement: Implement `solve(value, low, high)`. If `low` is greater than `high`, return the string `value-error`. Otherwise return `value` limited to the inclusive range: `low` when `value` is below it, `high` when `value` is above it, and `value` when it is inside. Use comparisons. Do not call min or max if you want the comparison practice, though a correct min/max after the bounds check also passes.
hints: Reject inverted bounds before you clamp.
One comparison against low and one against high cover the three regions.
Return the number itself when it is already inside. Do not return a string on success.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Clamp is the boundary pattern behind scores, pagination limits, and timeouts.

editorial: Clamp is the boundary pattern behind scores, pagination limits, and timeouts. The illegal case is low greater than high, which is a caller bug, not a value you can snap. Inclusive ends mean the endpoints are valid results.
